note: Saturday weekend run, 26 Sep 2026 07:02 SGT -- latest completed US session is Fri 25 Sep close: S&P +0.51% to 7,743.41, Nasdaq +0.48% to 27,068.72, Dow +0.93% to 51,828.62 (snapping a 3-week losing streak), VIX eased to ~14.9, even as the 10-year Treasury yield pushed to 5.18%, its highest since 2008. Equities rallying while yields hit a post-2008 high is the key cross-current: the dominant driver remains a live ~7-month US-Iran war, with Iran issuing a fresh 4-5 day ultimatum on Hormuz reopening on 24 Sep (expiring ~Mon-Tue 28-29 Sep) and Houthi strikes on Saudi Aramco's Yanbu hub on 25 Sep, while Brent eased to ~$105.3 and WTI to ~$92.7 on truce-hope headlines. Gold/silver extended Wednesday's pullback into Friday (gold ~$4,265/oz, silver ~$63.5/oz) on a firmer dollar and the higher real-yield backdrop. Sentiment ticked up marginally (CNN Fear&Greed 37/Fear, from 36) on the equity rally, with breadth internals improving modestly off Thursday's oversold McClellan reading but still net-bearish. The freshest BofA/EPFR Flow Show (week ended 23 Sep) showed a sharp reversal: US equity funds -$21.1bn and global equity funds -$10.2bn, versus +$63.8bn the prior week -- an early tell that fund positioning is starting to react to the hawkish-Fed repricing even as the cash index rallied Friday.
